description: Reverse-order, same-binary 512 then 256 row P2P served comparison; complements qwen36-p2p-512-chunk-ab.json.
method: The same server binary and environment were used for each arm, except Q36_P2P_CHUNK. The 512-row candidate ran first, the 256-row control second. Per arm: one 64-token cold warmup; three cold 524-token prompts; three cold 4274-token prompts; three deterministic 128-token decode samples. Server job-start-to-first-token timing includes first-token generation; client timing includes the complete reply. Correct arithmetic answers and matching decode output hashes were checked.

memory_reference.note: 256 MiB is a planning allowance, not a measured upper bound for the 512-row allocation; the new server must also pass its own admission and the 1 GiB live guard.

short.timing_note: Server timing runs from job start to first emitted batch and includes first-token generation; client timing runs to the complete reply.

long.timing_note: Server timing runs from job start to first emitted batch and includes first-token generation; client timing runs to the complete reply.

limits: The measured server is the parent integration commit; this MR adds test-only code and evidence.
This is the candidate-first half of two separate three-sample-per-arm runs, not a randomized or long-running performance study.
Configured 262144 context is not a 128k/256k prompt, retrieval or coding-quality test.
Both arms use experimental chunking and disable prefix reuse; neither arm represents the live eager service.
The 512-row physical-peer parity fixture has two synthetic layers and checks only final greedy winner and top-two logits.
The guard sampled VRAM and activity; sampled floors cannot exclude an unsampled transient. The confirmed router-poll exception cannot prove no hidden user request.
No setting was enabled or deployed by this experiment.
